correctness.rationale: For a deterministic SPD problem and a nonterminal Lanczos step, the Gaussian images of the basis and residual direction are independent. The sketched matrix is T plus a last-column rank-one update. Its terminal coefficient solves (1+D)Q=c with c the nonzero signed product of the Lanczos subdiagonals divided by det T. After a column rotation toward T^{-1}e_k, projecting out k-1 columns leaves s-k+1 Gaussian directions; the scalar regression is eta times an independent standard normal divided by a chi variable of those degrees of freedom. The resulting scaled Student density is continuous and positive at -1. The symmetric small interval defining |Q|>R has length 2|c|/R; integrating its density gives the stated constant and the moment cutoff. The vector error is at least the absolute error in that coordinate, and subtracting its deterministic exact-solution value does not cure divergence. At beta=0 full sketch rank gives the original invariant-subspace inverse. This checks the proof also at s=k (one residual degree of freedom); it does not extend to conditioned sketches, finite arithmetic, or harmonic projection. Read VERIFICATION.md and verify.py; their reported rational tests and scalar quadrature are corroboration, not a fresh replay or a proof of the Gaussian law.

evidence: The October 18 record gives an all-width/all-nonterminal-step regression representation and exact energy-error tail and moment cutoff. The October 26 record gives the complete vector law, energy-error tail, both sides of the moment cutoff, and comparison with minimal residual.

Güttel–Liu–Nyman (11) describes the method; successful-embedding guarantees are not unconditional moment bounds. Timsit–Grigori–Balabanov Proposition 3.1 and Fig. 1 give conditional quasi-optimality and observed spikes, not this exact law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Stronger indexed vector and error claims subsume the noninvariant case; invariance is the ordinary deterministic exactness of Galerkin on an invariant subspace. Published projection analyses were not the decisive coverage.

evidence: From the vector formula, a^Tg has scale eta/sqrt(s-k+1); integrating its Student density over |1+a^Tg|<|c|/R gives exactly 2|c|rho_nu. Energy-error moments diverge for p>=1 and the energy and Euclidean norms are equivalent for fixed SPD A.
The k=1 formula and the published rank-one sketched-Arnoldi framework alone do not assert the full higher-step Gaussian tail.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: All nontrivial parts are direct consequences of the distinct all-step record, with no independent classification left after taking its terminal projection. The dates do not establish authorship or scientific priority.

evidence: The October 26 proof gives y_F=y_0-c_* H^{-1}g/(1+a^Tg), with c_*=beta e_k^T y_0 and a=beta H^{-1}e_k, on the identical deterministic SPD Gaussian sketch. Taking the last coordinate gives (e_k^T y_0)/(1+a^Tg), with H=T for the frozen notation.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed October 26 finding gives the complete same-method random vector, including the Gaussian-regression law and the same rank-one pole. Projecting its formula on e_k gives exactly the frozen law for all admissible k,s; a one-dimensional density limit yields the stated coefficient. Its stronger energy-error moment cutoff implies the Euclidean divergence by SPD norm equivalence. This is demonstrated current coverage, not evidence that the October 26 record preceded the October 13 record. The October 13 one-step record alone does not cover k>=2.
residual_risks: Catalog dates and available passages do not establish historical priority; the decision reflects demonstrable existing coverage, not chronological precedence.

value.rationale: As a mathematical statement the error barrier is informative: it isolates why even a well-conditioned SPD problem can have infinite unconditional mean inverse error at every finite oversampling despite high-probability guarantees. The decision against the frozen finding is due to existing coverage, not lack of a meaningful stability question.
